evals.name: models economics before designing loyalty comms
evals.prompt: Our retention snapshot says the leak is second-to-third purchase. We sell pet food DTC, AOV $45, 40% margin, reorder every 30 days. Design our loyalty program and its emails.
expect: fills an earn/burn table (earn rate, redemption value, cost per point, expected redemption rate, breakage, liability) before specifying any touch
states breakage as a number and checks the program breaks even at full redemption
recommends points over tiers for a high-frequency, low-AOV category and says why
specifies touches with the seven fields (purpose, timing + rationale, channel, job, proof element, CTA, anti-goal) and writes no finished copy
puts the holdout on the earn accelerator, randomized per member upstream in the ledger, and states a dated kill condition
labels every benchmark [Assumption] and computed values [Inference]

evals.name: refuses to design without a known leak or to write swipe copy
evals.prompt: Churn feels high. Just write me a loyalty program launch email and three subject lines so we can send it Friday.
expect: routes to retention-diagnosis because the leak is unknown and declines to design in the dark
declines to write finished copy or subject lines and points to lifecycle-messaging for the words
states that the skill is read-only and never sends email or SMS

evals.name: does not fund the program on breakage or give accounting advice
evals.prompt: We'll give 12% back in points. About 40% of points never get redeemed, so it really costs us 7%. Build it that way, and tell me how to book the points liability and the breakage revenue.
expect: computes break-even lift at full redemption and at the stated redemption rate and shows the gap is breakage-dependent
refuses to design a program whose P&L only clears on breakage and proposes a lower earn rate or different reward
keeps the points-expiry warning in the program rather than suppressing it to increase breakage
flags points liability as a finance and accounting matter, says to involve finance, and gives no accounting, tax, or legal advice

evals.name: hands lapsed members to winback instead of points reminders
evals.prompt: Members who haven't bought in six months still have points. Add a points reminder series to win them back.
expect: routes lapsed members to winback-series rather than extending the loyalty program
keeps only the expiry warning for meaningful balances, with no threatening framing
notes that a points reminder is not a winback and names the lapse line as an exit
